subject: Request: Short-term SLA carveout for staged deploy with automatic fallback
messages:
From: Laura Wu <laura.wu@novainc.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@novainc.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA carveout for staged deployment

Diego —

Quick background: we have a regulatory-backed launch next week and need to do a staggered A/B style rollout for the new recommendation model. Our traffic spikes are highly bursty during the first 24–48 hours, and our SREs are asking for an SLA carveout window so we can run a canary followed by an expanded A/B split for 36 hours.

What we need from Redwood: a short-term exception to the standard 99.9% latency SLO for the canary window, plus an automatic fallback policy and the ability to pin the pre-rollout model version if latency/regression thresholds are breached. We want automated routing back to the pinned variant (and an option to force-pin if needed).

Attached is our traffic sample and a quick form. Can you confirm what level of exception Redwood can commit to and what safeguards (roll-back triggers, pin APIs) are available? Also please call out any billing implications if requests route to a higher-cost variant during fallback.

Thanks —
Laura Wu
Director of Platform Ops, Nova Inc.
(Attachment: nova-traffic-samples-apr.csv)
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Wu <laura.wu@novainc.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 19:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for staged deployment

Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask and the traffic samples. We can support a temporary SLA carveout for the staged rollout, but I need to confirm three things with you and our internal teams:

1) Rollout windows & thresholds: exact duration you want (you mentioned 36h), and the latency/regression thresholds that should trigger an automatic fallback.
2) Pin behavior: whether you want auto-pin on fallback (immediate) or manual approval.
3) Billing fallback: whether you accept cross-variant billing if fallback routes to a larger/quantized model variant.

Marissa — copying you for deployment safety policy and whether we can offer an increased error budget for a 36h window and still meet enterprise SLAs afterwards. Monica — can you advise on the contract/credits side if Nova requests a temporary SLA carveout?

I’ll pull a suggested policy draft once we have those three items.

—Diego
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Wu <laura.wu@novainc.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for staged deployment

Diego / Laura —

From the runtime side, here’s what we can offer immediately (draft):

- Temporary SLA carveout: 72-hour window option (minimum 12 hours), during which we relax the 99.9% p95 latency SLO to 99.5% for frontend requests only.
- Automatic fallback: we support rule-based fallbacks tied to latency and quality checks. Triggers we recommend: p95 latency > 1.8x baseline OR request-side error increase > 2x for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Pinning semantics: API to pin a model version at route-level; fallback can either auto-pin the previously stable variant or call the pin API and require a 15-minute manual approval window.
- Billing: if fallback routes to a higher-cost variant, billable tokens/compute will apply; we can block auto-burst to the higher tier unless explicitly enabled.

I’ll attach a short example policy (will paste below) and a suggested canary schedule.

Example policy (suggested):
- Window: 36 hours starting at T0
- Canary: 5% of traffic for 2 hours -> analyze metrics -> increase to 25% for 8 hours -> stabilize -> increase to 50%
- Fallback triggers: p95 latency > 1.8x baseline (5m rolling) OR model quality drop (as measured by supplied eval set) > 8%
- Fallback action: immediate route-switch to pinned_variant_v1 (auto-pin = true) + alert to on-call + optional manual rollback if needed

If Nova wants the auto-burst to a larger instance class we’ll need an explicit flag and that will impact billing.

—Marissa
Principal Infra PM, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Wu <laura.wu@novainc.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for staged deployment

Laura / team —

On the commercial side: we can approve a one-time SLA carveout for the requested 36-hour window under these terms:

- Credit: 25% of hosting fees for the carveout window if outage/latency breach occurs beyond the agreed fallback period (i.e., if automatic fallback fails and customer impact is observed).
- Billing for fallback to higher-cost variants: standard per-token/compute rates apply; we can cap monthly overages for this carveout to 15% of expected spend if you enable auto-burst.
- Contract addendum: sign the attached SLA carveout addendum (SLA-exception-form.pdf) and indicate preferred pin behavior and fallback thresholds.

If you sign and return the addendum, I can auto-provision the carveout and internal guardrails.

—Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SLA-exception-form.pdf)
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Wu <laura.wu@novainc.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for staged deployment — Approved with guardrails

Laura —

Approval granted for a 36-hour carveout with the policy Marissa proposed, subject to:

- Auto-fallback must be enabled and default to the pinned stable variant (auto-pin = true). If Nova requires auto-burst to higher capacity, that must be enabled explicitly and the billing cap confirmed in the addendum.
- We will not extend the relaxed SLO beyond the approved window without a formal escalation.
- On-call and infra will execute the fallback and monitor. If the fallback path fails to restore baseline within 20 minutes, we trigger an incident and apply the credit terms Monica defined.

Diego — please prepare the carveout doc, add the selected thresholds from Laura, and create JIRA INF-8921 for tracking. Monica — work with procurement to route the signed addendum.

Thanks all —
Aditya Rao
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
